Planning read of orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's cycle_plan_dispatch_hash() surfaced a STANDING OBLIGATION that invalidated the research report's Recommendation 2 (emit the plan's mtime at dispatch-build time): the implement agent checks off plan items every cycle, so an mtime/sha line in the implement dispatch block would have permanently rendered the IDENTICAL DISPATCH HALT inert unless orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (contended with 5 other tasks) were also edited. The plan was redesigned to emit only static content, which is also the better design since the correct freshness baseline is the agent's own first read, not dispatch-build time.

Observed live in the same batch that shipped this task's remedy: an uncovered variant of the exact hazard it addresses. A planner-agent reported its plan complete, the orchestrator postflighted and committed that plan, then the SAME planner-agent continued editing the plan in place (renaming a phase from 'Correct the Two Durable Records' to 'Correct the Three Durable Records', adding scope, 6.25h to 6.5h) after reporting. No .plan-revised.json sentinel was written, because the sentinel-writing obligation added by this task lives in reviser-agent.md (reached via the aux plan-revision dispatch path) and in general-implementation-agent.md as the reader -- planner-agent.md carries no such obligation. The dispatch side worked correctly: the implement dispatch file DID carry the revision_sentinel pointer, so the implementer was instructed to check for a sentinel that by construction could never appear for this revision path. No correctness harm occurred in this instance purely by timing luck: the plan's last write preceded the dispatch-file build by 0.7s, so the dispatch file and the subsequently-spawned implementer both saw the revised plan. Had the planner's edit landed after the implementer's read, the implementer would have silently executed a superseded plan with the sentinel check passing vacantly. Also note the revision left the committed plan stale relative to the working tree (the committed copy still said 'Two Durable Records'), since the postflight commit had already fired. Suggested follow-up: either extend the sentinel-writing obligation to planner-agent.md for post-report in-place edits, or make the plan-report boundary authoritative so a planner cannot edit after reporting.
